author: Autodesk
documentation:
This basic infection graph is used simulate property growth on a set of points. It's a weighted-average by distance system that can mimic the spread of an infection in a medium. It's build around a solver, so you will need to reset the solver by returning to a frame **before** the start_frame listed on the compound. ### `object_to_infect` The points object input. Points object only. ### ***Point Generation*** * **Infection Points:**
The number of initial infected points. * **Random Seed:**
Seed for the random number generator that chooses the initial infection points. * **Use Custom Infection Points:**
Instead of using the internal seed points generator, the solver reads the point positions from the `custom_seed_positions` input. `custom_seed_positions` is a float3 input and can be connected to internal bifrost values or float3 values passed in from your scene. ### ***Infection Settings*** * **Infection Property:**
The name of the main infection property, this will grow across the frame range allowing it to be used to drive animations, scales, colors etc. * **Normalized Infection Property:**
The same as above, but mapped to a 0-1 range. * **Start Frame:**
The starting frame of the solver, The initial settings will be applied at frames below this number. * **Initial Infection Value:**
Starting value of the ***Infection Property***. * **Neighbor Count:**
As the solver runs over the points, it looks for neighbors of the current point and reads their ***Infection Property*** values. This controls how many neighbors it looks at. This, combined with the ***Infection Spread*** property, controls how fast the infection propogates. * **Infection Spread:**
This is the radius in which the solver looks for point infection values. Higher values can cause the solver to slow down. This, combined with the ***Neighbor Count*** property, controls how fast the infection propogates. * **Infection Intensity:**
This controls how much of the distance between points is taken into account. It has the effect of controlling how fast the intensity of the infection grows. * **Additional Infection Points:**
Add n additional new infection points. This adds new infection points on every step of the solver. This is useful in the situation where your infection must be total. * **Additional Infection Frame:**
Allows you to set the frame after which the new infection points are added. * **Max Infection Value:**
The highest your infection intensity can be. ### ***Diagnostic*** * **Point Size:**
Point size on screen. * **Show Radius Sample:**
When switched on, it will display the **Infection Spread** as a circle. This is the radius that the solver looks in to find neighbors. Only shows this on the starting points. * **Infection Color:**
All uninfected points **always** are drawn as black. Anything with an infection property above zero will be drawn in this color. * **Intensity Color:**
As the intensity of the infection grows, the color of the point will grow to be this color. ### ***Outputs*** * **All Points:**
Outputs all the points with properties * **Infected Points:**
Outputs only the points with an infection value above zero

_notes.text:
# Input points

Replace with your points
Infection solver inside!

# Custom points

The infection solver lets you set which points you wish to start the infection from.  These are those positions.

# press play

To see the infection at work

# ***Note***
This compound uses a memory cache.  This means that as the infection runs, the frames are cached to memory.  To reset the cache and recalculate, press ***CTRL-R*** or from the edit menu, ***Reset Feedback State***

Failure to do this may result in incorrect output.

# Create the initial array

The initial infection array is created based on the number of incoming points, and set to all zeros.  It then has the starting points infection values set in it to go to the solver.

# Infection Start Points

Here you can choose between setting custom points or generating random points to begin your infection.

# Setup the properties

The infection system has 2 major properties, the infection property itself, and a normalized version of the infection property.  These can be used post sim.

# The Infection Solver

Is a weighted-average by distance system that can mimic the spread of an infection in a medium. The infection solver checks the neighbors of the infected points each frame, calculates the distance to those neighbors and sets a new infection value for those points based on their distance to the initial infection point.

Please dive into the solver for a more complete explanation.

# Display the Results

This is where the user sets colours and display properties for output to the viewport and Arnold for rendering.

# Remove non-infected points

If the user only wants to retrieve the points that are infected, this section deletes all points who have an infection property of zero.

# Additional Points
The solver has the ability to add random points to the infection during the sequence, this controls when that process starts.

# Should Simulate
The ***should_simulate*** compound controls when the simulation starts based on the *start_frame* input.

# Get the data from last frame
A solver uses the results of it's last frame to start calculations on the current frame.  In this section, the data for the infection is retrieved and any additional random points are points are added by having their infection value adjusted.  The infection value is retreived from the incoming point object and added to if additional random points are specified.

# Weighted Average by Distance
This is where the magic happens.  The information is all read into this for loop (double-click for more info) where the neighbor information is used to find the distance to each of the points' neighbors within a radius.   This is used to average the infection value among all the neighbors and add them to the current point.

# Set properties for next solver step
The result of the weighted average is clamped to the *max_infection* value and applied to the points object.

# Normalized values
The results of the weighted average are conformed to a 0-1 range for output to the object's *normalized_infection* property
Taking the current point position and the positions of the current points' neighbors, a distance is calculated and conformed to the *infection_intensity* input
The neighbors infection value is multiplied by the result of the distance calculation above.  This result is averaged and added to the infection value of the current point.

# memory_cache

This compound caches the ***infection_solver*** to memory, so that Arnold can render it.

The graph needs to be played through first to cache the solver in memory.

If this is not done, the render will not be accurate.

# 3d

In this section, points are scattered inside a spherical volume.
